patch.value: Declared intent token budgets are smaller than the smallest projection their own command can emit, so three of five intents return no result at all on this tracker

The intent layer now enforces its declared budgets at one egress point, and enforcement works. What was never checked is whether a declared budget is reachable. Measured at HEAD on the live 2,215-item tracker: next:execute declares 1200 tokens and its smallest bounded projection measures 1438, so the result is dropped on every invocation. context:orient declares 2400 and its smallest bounded section set measures 8417, a factor of 3.5, and it is still dropped at an explicit 8000. context:handoff declares 2200 and behaves identically. Two further reachable cases have no override at all: pm list --limit 200 --for triage and pm get <id> --depth deep --for inspect both drop the result, and --token-budget exits 2 unknown_option on list, get and search, so the ceiling cannot be raised. Run the same five intents against a two-item sandbox workspace and every one of them fits: next:execute measures 367 of 1200 and context:orient 583 of 2400. The declared numbers were therefore calibrated against a toy corpus, and the product targets millions of items. Three separate contract failures follow. First, degradation is all-or-nothing: the only tier below the full projection is budget_receipt_only, which carries zero rows, so there is no graded descent from many rows to fewer rows. Second, the receipt is self-contradictory: within_budget reports true while budget_exceeded.omitted_result reports true in the same envelope, because the estimate is measured after the payload was deleted, so the only way the receipt is within budget is that nothing was served. Third, the recovery guidance says to repeat the command without --for, which routes the caller to the unprojected form: pm next --json is 12,879 bytes against a 400-byte omission receipt, so the documented escape from a token ceiling costs 32 times more tokens than the failure it escapes.

Every declared intent budget is greater than or equal to the measured minimum bounded projection of its own command on a corpus at least the size of the current tracker, and a gate fails the build when it is not; Budget enforcement offers at least one intermediate tier that still carries rows before omission is permitted, and the receipt names the tier actually applied; A response that omits its result never reports within_budget true, and the receipt distinguishes an infeasible declaration from an exceeded one; Recovery guidance for an infeasible budget never instructs a caller to re-run the unprojected command when that form emits more tokens than the projection it replaces; The published evidence table records declared budget, measured minimum projection and applied degradation per intent on both a two-item corpus and the current tracker, so calibration against a toy corpus is visible in review

author: harness:claude-code
message: Calibrating a reachable ceiling depends on the final envelope cost, so per-page amortisation lands first or the calibration is done twice against two different envelopes

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Method that found this, reusable for any declared bound: run the identical invocation against a two-item workspace and against the real tracker, and diff the verdicts rather than the outputs. A bound that is satisfied on the small corpus and violated on the large one is a scalar that should have been a function, and the small corpus is the one the number was authored against. A bound violated on both is an ordinary miscalibration. A bound satisfied on both is genuinely scale-invariant and can be left alone.

Second technique, for the same class: a floor is invisible from the default. Raising the ceiling in steps until content first appears is the only way to measure the smallest form a command can emit, because at the default the response contains no rows to measure. next execute yielded nothing at 1200 and 2000 and content at 4000, which located the floor between 2000 and 4000 and then exactly at 1438 from the receipt. Doing this in the other direction, lowering a working ceiling until output disappears, gives the same number and is cheaper when the default already works.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Still live at HEAD 2026.7.31, verified 2026-07-31. `pm next --for execute` emits budget_exceeded.omitted_result: true alongside within_budget: true in one envelope, with token_budget 1200 and estimated_tokens 79 — the receipt reports the omitted-result payload as within budget, so the two keys in the same envelope assert opposite things. The recovery instruction "Repeat the original command without --for" costs 9,259 bytes against the 320-byte refusal.
